chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:
"When the slave performs Hajj and is then freed, he must repeat Hajj."
ai.seo_question: Does a slave need to perform Hajj again after being freed?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that the Hajj performed by a slave is valid but distinct from the obligatory Hajj (Hajjat al-Islam) required of a free person. Consequently, upon manumission, the individual must perform a new Hajj to fulfill the specific religious duty attached to their new status of freedom, a ruling derived from the conditions of financial independence and freedom from bondage inherent in the pillar. This distinction underscores the Shia view that the validity of obligatory acts can be contingent upon the performer's specific legal status at the time of execution.
